adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the object schema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the string `"[object Object]"`, so both computed keys collapse to the same literal property name and the second overwrites the first. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from `z.string().toString()` so it requires a nonsense key of type number and strips all real fields; with sync enabled every refresh throws "Invalid refreshed tokens", and the schema does not actually validate the untrusted sync response.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, the computed property names use `z.string().toString()` (and `z.string().optional().toString()`), which are evaluated immediately to a single literal string key (whatever Zod’s `toString()` returns), not a “catch-all”/dynamic key. That makes the schema require (or define) a fixed, nonsensical property name rather than accepting arbitrary numeric expiry fields like `expires_in`/`expiry_date`. As a result, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is true, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` will typically fail for real token responses, causing `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to throw `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned` on every refresh. This is a concrete correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The credential-sync validation branch has no test with a normal token payload, so the computed "[object Object]" required key can reject every refresh response and break token renewal.
